about.title: About EarthChestra
about.intro: EarthChestra turns NASA Earth observations into orchestral music. Choose a place on Earth, listen to how its climate has changed, and watch the data light up on the globe as the music plays.
about.howZone: Choose a zone on the globe or in the list: a continent, a country, an ocean or a sea.
about.howTracks: Choose the datasets to hear in the Audio Tracks panel. Each dataset is played by its own instrument.
about.howPlay: Press Play. Each dataset is averaged over your zone, month by month, and every month becomes one bar of music.
about.howPitch: Higher values play higher notes, measured against your zone's own range, so a value always gives the same note.
about.howLoudness: More rain or lightning sounds louder and busier; snow only plays when it snows.
about.howGlobe: While the music plays, the globe shows the data of your zone: one colour per dataset, and the stronger the value, the more solid the dot. Select Change zone or press Escape to pick another zone.
about.orchestraText: Each dataset has its own instrument:
about.dataText: All datasets are placed on one common map grid of 0.25° (about 28 km), so a place has the same position in every dataset.

sources.gistemp: surface temperature anomaly compared with the 1951–1980 average, monthly since 1880.
sources.imerg: rain and snow from the Global Precipitation Measurement mission, monthly averages since June 2000.
sources.lis: lightning seen by the Lightning Imaging Sensor on the International Space Station, March 2017 to July 2023.
sources.nightLights: night lights, one map per year from 2012 to 2023.
sources.co2: carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere, in parts per million, September 2002 to March 2022.
sources.naturalEarth: outlines of continents, countries, oceans and seas (public domain).

about.techFrontend: Web app: React, TypeScript and Vite. The 3D globe uses react-globe.gl (three.js), and the sound plays through the Web Audio API.
about.techBackend: Music: a Python service (FastAPI) writes an orchestral score (MIDI) for your zone and renders it to audio with orchestral samples, in short pieces that play back to back.
about.techData: Globe: the browser reads the same monthly data maps (NumPy files) straight from the server and downloads only the part that covers your zone.
about.techDeploy: Deployment: Docker Compose runs the web app (nginx), the music service and a container that installs the datasets.
about.a11yText: EarthChestra aims to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. All controls can be used with the keyboard. In the player, Space plays or pauses, the arrow keys move through time, Home and End jump to the start or the end, and M mutes. During playback, Escape returns to zone selection. The List View is a screen-reader-friendly alternative to the globe, the values shown on the globe are also available as a table, and status changes are announced.
about.teamText: Built at HEIG-VD (Yverdon-les-Bains, Switzerland) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
about.teamMembers: Magali Egger, Téo Ferrari, Clarisse Estelle Fleurimont, Yasaman Izadmehr, Simon Walther and Léo Zmoos.
